name: b-fireside-public-information
prompt: A still frame from a faded 1970s home-safety broadcast, shot on grainy 16mm reversal film: a lone figure sits upright in a high-backed wingback armchair upholstered in rust velour, in a snug suburban sitting room after dark. Behind the chair the wall is papered in big interlocking circles of burnt orange, chocolate brown and mustard. To one side a tall standard lamp with a pleated fabric shade throws warm tungsten light down across the chair, leaving the corners of the room in soft brown shadow. On a small side table at the figure's elbow, a cup and saucer of milky tea rests on a white lace doily. The figure wears a plain charcoal hand-knitted ski mask covering the whole head and neck, tucked into a dark roll-neck jumper; around the wearer's left eye hole a thin white ring is knitted into the wool, and inside that ring, at about two o'clock, sits a small red triangle with softly rounded corners, point down. The eyes sit in shadow inside the holes. Black leather gloves rest flat and patient on both armrests. Medium close-up from the chest up, camera at eye level and dead square to the sitter, who stares straight down the lens with the mild, reassuring patience of someone about to explain the weekly household budget. Slightly soft focus, visible organic grain, a little gate weave, highlights blooming gently around the lampshade, warm reds and oranges pushed rich while the paler tones wash out towards cream, deep crushed blacks, a gentle dark vignette at the edges. Portrait framing, no text or lettering anywhere. Thanks.
